lines.text: Every storm eventually finds the boat you're already in.
And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship.
Jesus was asleep in the stern, undisturbed by the chaos around him.
Master, carest thou not that we perish?
He stood. He didn't grab an oar. He didn't bail water.
And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
The same voice is still in the boat with you tonight.
Peace was never the absence of waves. It's the presence of the One who made them.

bold: Peace was never the absence of waves. It's the presence of the One who made them.
title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: Peace, Be Still
story: A storm-tossed boat at night under lightning and rain, calmed when a figure stands as black clouds split by gold light, resting at last into a rose-gold sunrise at sea - the story of Mark 4:35-41, and what it means to trust the same voice that's still in the boat with you before the waves actually stop.
